svg.title: How Whisper turns speech into text
svg.desc: How Whisper turns audio into text. Audio is resampled to 16,000 samples a second and cut into 30-second windows. Each window becomes a log-Mel spectrogram (80 pitch bands, 25 ms slices). An encoder reads the spectrogram. A decoder then writes tokens one at a time: first a language token, then a task token (transcribe or translate), then whether to add timestamps, then the text. Silence gets its own no-speech token. Long audio is done one window after another, moving the window forward by the timestamps the model predicted.
svg.text: How Whisper turns speech into text

g.text: 2. Turn one window into a spectrogram
3. The encoder reads it, the decoder writes tokens one at a time
instruction tokens first, then the words
silent window? it writes a “no speech” token instead
4. Long audio: move the window forward by the timestamps it predicted, and repeat

svg.text: Mechanism from Radford et al., “Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision” (OpenAI, 2022). Spectrogram drawn for illustration, not data.
